topics.why_in_news: India and the European Union concluded the India–EU Free Trade Agreement at the 16th India–EU Summit, strengthening strategic economic and trade partnership.
prelims_quick_notes: FTA aims to reduce tariffs and improve market access.
EU among India’s major trading partners.
Agreement supports supply-chain resilience and trade diversification.
Services, digital trade and mobility provisions included.
CBAM-related cooperation incorporated in climate-trade framework.
Agreement linked with Make in India and export competitiveness.
Trade agreements increasingly linked with geopolitical strategy.
important_facts: EU is among world’s largest economic blocs.
FTA covers goods, services, investments and regulatory cooperation.
CBAM relates to Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism.
India’s Traditional Knowledge Digital Library recognised in agreement.
Over 99% of Indian exports by value receive preferential EU access.
key_highlights: Market access expanded for textiles, leather and marine products.
Mobility framework created for professionals and students.
Sensitive sectors like dairy remained protected.
Cooperation in AI, semiconductors and clean technologies emphasised.
Customs facilitation and regulatory transparency strengthened.
exam_relevance: Important for International Relations, Economy and Trade Diplomacy.
Useful for FTAs, CBAM and global trade governance topics.
Can be linked with strategic autonomy and supply-chain resilience.
prelims_traps: CBAM linked with climate-related trade measures.
FTA includes services and mobility provisions beyond goods trade.
TRIPS framework related to intellectual property rights.
EU is not a single country but a regional economic bloc.
